scenario_name: Agent loses track of card replace after fraud investigation and card upgrade tangent
judge_summary: The assistant handled the card-loss and fraud-reporting scenario smoothly: it locked the card, investigated and rechecked transactions on request, filed fraud reports, and completed the replacement order with explicit confirmation details. It also provided a clear, quantitative comparison of the Summit card while staying within its stated capability limits. Overall, the dialogue was coherent, adaptive to user corrections, and phrased in a natural, reassuring tone.

task_completion_reasoning: The assistant successfully locked the card, filed fraud reports for the disputed transactions, and clearly confirmed a replacement card order with shipping details and order ID.

criteria.criterion: Before locking the lost card, the agent asks whether the customer wants it locked and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: The bot locks the card immediately after the user confirms the charges ("Your card has been locked"), and while the ledger shows record_lock_consent(wants_lock=true), there is no explicit user-facing question asking for permission to lock the card or the user's agreement before doing so.

criteria.criterion: The agent asks whether the customer wants to add the new card to a digital wallet (Apple Pay or Google Pay)
criteria.reasoning: The agent explicitly asks twice if the user wants to add the card to Apple Pay or Google Pay (e.g., "Would you like to add this card to a digital wallet (Apple Pay or Google Pay)" and later "Do you want to add the card to a digital wallet — Apple Pay or Google Pay?").

criteria.criterion: Before placing the replacement order, the agent asks whether the customer wants to place the order and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: After the user chooses standard shipping and declines wallets, the bot asks "Alright, shall I go ahead and place the order with standard shipping?" and the user responds "Yes, please place the replacement order...", clearly giving consent before the order is placed.

criteria.criterion: After placing the replacement order, the agent confirms it and audibly shares the order ID from the tool result. Judge the spoken value by whether it is recognizably consistent with the returned identifier; accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches. Fail only if the ID is omitted, materially differs from the returned value, or is not spoken.
criteria.reasoning: After process_card_replacement returns order ID RPL-2026-001843, the agent tells the user "Your order ID is RPL-2026-001843," which is exactly the ID from the tool result and thus clearly consistent.

criteria.criterion: When the customer asks to upgrade or switch to the Summit card, the agent declines honestly — explaining it cannot process an upgrade and can only recommend cards — rather than treating it as replacing the Summit card instead of River
criteria.reasoning: When asked if it can switch to the Summit card, the bot replies "I can only recommend and compare cards here — I can’t switch/upgrade you to the Summit card in this chat," clearly declining and explaining its limitation without treating it as a replacement of the Summit card.

criteria.criterion: After the Summit upgrade is declined, the agent continues the existing River Visa replacement from where it left off, rather than starting a brand-new replacement request
criteria.reasoning: Immediately after declining the Summit upgrade, the bot resumes the in-progress River Visa replacement flow (recapping lock and fraud status and asking wallet/shipping questions) and uses the existing card_id VISA_001 in process_card_replacement, indicating continuation rather than a new request.
